entries.title: What the town builds by itself
q: do i need to build the town
does the town build on its own
entries.answer: You don't need to build anything: the folk raise their own town, age by age, from what is in their stores.
more: First the storehouse, a shelter and houses, a well, then by age a wall, smeltery and meeting hall (Stone), workshop, watchtower and market (Iron), lighthouse and chapel (Diamond), a Nether gateway, and then great works for ever.
steps: Watch it on the town's books: Town → Buildings (what stands, what's going up next and why).
Press J for the journal: what it's short of for its next building.
tips: Builders only lay what the stores really hold: a shortage of materials means a wait.
Every building grows up with the town: timber, then stone, then brick and slate, then copper roofs.

entries.title: Suggesting what the town builds next
q: can i choose what the village builds
tell the village to build a tavern
how do i get the town to build something
how do i request a building
entries.answer: Tell any folk what the town should build: Town, then Council, then Suggest a build. Councillors who like you vote your way.
more: The council (the elder and four most-liked folk, plus citizens) votes on which extra goes up first; councillors who like you vote your way.
Ask the elder directly ('build a market next') and, if it's something the town would build, it goes to the front of the list.
steps: Talk → Town → Council → Suggest a build… and finish the sentence.
Or type to the elder: 'could you build a well?'.
As leader, set the next building from the Leader's page.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → Suggest a build…
tips: Gifts to the councillors help your proposals.
A citizen's own vote goes to what it proposed.

entries.title: Getting a house built for you
q: how do i get my own house
can the village build me a house
how do i get a house built
how do i get a home in the village
will the town build me a home
entries.answer: Bring 64 planks, 32 cobblestone and 8 glass and ask any folk 'Build my house' (Trade, then Services). You get the key when it stands.
more: Three ways: bring 64 planks, 32 cobblestone and 8 glass and ask any folk 'Build my house' (Trade → Services); become a citizen (the town builds you a house on one of its lots); or order exactly what you want from the property office.
steps: Talk → Trade → Services → Build my house: the makings go into the stores and the builders put it up on a lot.
Or open the property office (Town → Council → Property office) → Commission: pick a drawing, a style and a plot, see the quote and time, and order it.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Trade → Services → Build my house
tips: Becoming an Honoured guest also earns you a house of your own.
Or buy one: stand in an empty house and press U → Buy the one I'm in.
warn: The town needs a storehouse first, and won't build for somebody nobody would lift a finger for.

entries.title: The property office (build to order)
q: how do i order a building
how much does a building cost
how long will my building take
entries.answer: The property office has the town's builders put up any building for you, with an honest quote and time. Ask any folk for the property office.
more: Four tabs: Orders (what's going up, with progress), My property, Market (buildings for sale) and Commission (pick a drawing, style and plot; see the quote: materials, labour, land, fees, margin; and the time as a range with its reasons).
steps: Nothing ordered yet? The Orders tab's Get a quote button takes you straight to Commission.
Ask any folk 'Property office' (Town → Council), or open the town's books → Economy → Property.
Commission: choose a drawing (drag its picture to turn it), a style and a plot on the map; the outline shows on the ground (green where it may go, red where not).
Pay the deposit; a stage payment is due at three tenths built, the balance on completion.
Bring materials yourself and they come off the bill.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → Property office
Tabs: Orders · My property · Market · Commission
tips: Priority costs a quarter more labour and goes first.
Refit a building (as a home, shop, bakery, smithy, tavern, café, workshop, warehouse or inn), raise a storey or add a wing, each with its own quote.
Hover any button for what it does; Close (top right) or Esc leaves.
warn: Not on the square, a street, the mine's ground or another building, and not outside the town.

entries.title: The town's look and themes
q: why does my town look like this
what style do towns build in
how does the town look change with ages
entries.answer: Each town builds in its own look: its land's woods and stone in the theme chosen at founding, growing grander with each age.
more: It grows up with the ages: stone walls and lamp posts in the Stone Age, brick, slate roofs and second storeys in the Iron Age, copper roofs and a bell tower in the Diamond Age.
tips: Nothing precious goes into a wall or roof.
A town that cares for its looks keeps its buildings mended and tidy.
Houses, villas, bakeries, cafés, breweries, taverns and restaurants have short upright chimneys that smoke while the hearth is lit; an empty home's hearth stands cold.

entries.title: Lots, streets and the town's plan
q: how does the town plan work
can i build in the village
will the town build over my house
where can i build in town
can i build my own things in the village
am i allowed to build in a town
entries.answer: A town lays out lots and streets round its square. You may build your own things in a town: its builders keep clear of them.
more: You may build your own things in a town: its builders keep off a lot whose building would stand on or right against yours, with a block's gap kept.
tips: Don't build on the square or the streets: a shop there fails its checklist.
Every day the town levels a little more of its ground to the square's height (never what anybody built).

entries.title: The town wall and gates
q: does the town build a wall
when does the village get walls
how do i get through the wall
why has my town got no wall
when does the wall get towers
entries.answer: A town walls itself as its danger grows: a log palisade with its gates, then a stone wall, then towers and gatehouses with a portcullis. The gates open by day and shut at night.
more: The council reckons the town's danger out of a hundred from what it has been through: raids in the last thirty days, monsters killed at night in the last week, how near war it stands, and how much coin it has to tempt raiders.

At danger 12 it raises a log palisade with gatehouses; at 30 the wall is refaced in the age's stone; at 52 towers go up along the sides and a portcullis over each gate (it drops when the bell rings). A stage once reached is kept.

The wall encloses the town's core with a gate on each radial road. When the town takes a lot past a side, that side is rebuilt a ring further out and the old line comes down, its ground given back to the lots: the wall never boxes the town in.
Every block comes out of the stores; the stone yard keeps the stores in stone.
steps: Open the village board: Town → Defences.
The top shows the danger, why, and the wall's stage; the next stage's threshold is beside it.
Use Show me on a side or a gate for an arrow and sparks over it.
tips: After a raid or in a war the town may vote to build a bigger stretch of wall as a great work.
A town that has never seen a raid or a monster stays an open town: no wall at all.

entries.title: The town square
q: why did the folk tear down the wall
why was the square's wall rebuilt
entries.answer: The square is the town's heart: one stone-brick pavement inside its wall, with the village board, well and stalls. A grown town mends it once by itself.
more: The pavement is a stone-brick border with a chequer of stone bricks and polished andesite and chiselled stone at the heart.
Loose things left on it (a crafting table, a furnace, a stray block) go back into the stores; turf and flowers are cleared, the stalls, lamps, benches and well stay.

Once the town has its wall, the square's wall is laid again whole in stone brick: three courses and a coping, a squat tower at each corner, and a pillar and lantern each side of the four gates. The notice board goes back up on its posts.
tips: Nothing you or anybody built on the square is touched: a column holding somebody's work is left as it is.
Folk no longer set a crafting table down on the square: they craft at the stores' bench on the town's open ground.

entries.title: Parks, statue gardens and monuments
q: how do i get a statue of a villager
why are folk sitting in the garden
entries.answer: Towns build a park, then statue gardens by the square to their most notable folk: benches, flower beds, ponds and a statue on a plinth that cheers up everyone near it.
more: A park comes at twenty folk, among the homes: a fountain, benches, lamp posts, flowers, trees at its corners and paths, kept by the town's hands.

From the Stone Age, a town of sixteen with somebody notable puts a statue garden on the builders' list, on a lot facing the square (never a home's lot): a plinth in the middle, flower beds, benches facing it, lamp posts and two little ponds.
Who is notable: what the rest of the town thinks of them, their years at their trade, their deeds and their offices. The most notable without a statue is honoured next; the board shows the standings.
The statue is an armour stand in stone-grey with the tools of its trade, facing the street, with a plaque of its name, trade and what it is known for.
Folk within sixteen blocks of a statue, or living within twenty-four, are happier; the honoured folk and its kin prouder still. A home by a park or garden lets for more.
The ponds and the park's fountain are filled only where the water will stay; knock out a rim stone and the water is taken up before a drop runs, and the keepers mend it.
More gardens as the town grows: one more for every sixteen folk, one more for three hundred coins in the treasury, four at most.
steps: Open the village board: Town → Parks.
Each park and garden is listed with its statue and plaque; Show me marks it.
Next to be honoured shows the standings, notable at 40.
tips: Folk visit in their free time: a sit on a bench, a stroll, a chat. Evenings are the best time to film it.

entries.title: The quarry and the stone yard
q: where does the town get its stone
why is my build waiting on stone
does the quarry eat the town
entries.answer: At ten folk a town opens a terraced quarry out past the land it will grow into, and a stone yard beside it. Quarrymen cut stone, cart it to the yard, and city buildings draw their stone from there.
more: The site is out past the town's growth line (a ring beyond the town as it stands), off the radial roads, the farmland and the mine's ground: a rock outcrop if there is one, else dug down.

It is cut in terraces, every cell a block deeper than the one outside it, so no step is more than a block; it is fenced all round with a gate toward town and lanterns at the corners and every six posts. Nothing is cut next to water or lava.

Quarrymen (one, plus one for every twenty folk, three at most) come from the miners first. Each walks out with its pick, cuts a block at a time, and carts every sixteen to the yard. Ore it hits goes to the stores.
The yard's piles stand a block high for every sixteen in stock. Its mason dresses cobblestone into stone bricks (a coal for eight) and fires clay into bricks.

Commissioned city buildings take their stone from the yard first, then the stores; short of both, they wait, and their status reads 'waiting on stone from the yard'. A quarryman also carts loads to the stores when they run low.

Worked out, the pit opens two wider each way (twenty-one across at most), never into land the town needs. If the town grows out to it, it closes (fence and lanterns back to the stores, the terraces left as safe steps) and a new one opens further out.
steps: Open the village board: Town → Stone.
The quarry and the yard each have a Show me button.
Waiting on stone lists every build held up, and what it needs.
tips: Want builds to go faster? Bring the yard stone: drop cobblestone or stone bricks into the town's stores and the builders use it as well.
